title: Martian Regolith & Iron Oxide
quickFact: Martian regolith contains 18% iron oxide (rust), creating the distinctive reddish sky and soil.
explore: Martian soil, known as regolith, is made of finely crushed basalt rock and iron-rich dust. Unlike Earth soil, it contains no organic matter, but NASA scientists have developed methods to smelt this regolith into structural alloy plates and microwave it into building bricks for planetary habitats.

refinementConversion.description: Smelted into structural alloy plates for outpost reinforcement.

checkQuestion.question: Why does Mars appear reddish-orange from space?
options: Volcanic lava flows covering the surface
High concentration of iron oxide (rust) in the soil
checkQuestion.explanation: Iron in the Martian surface minerals reacts with trace oxygen and atmospheric oxidizers to form iron(III) oxide—commonly known as rust.
